title: Deliverability + Suppression Plan (Lifecycle Growth Sprint)
content:
Purpose
- Ensure onboarding email sequence (welcome + quickstart + first-success + troubleshooting + next steps) launches without hurting domain reputation, triggering spam filters, or violating opt-out expectations.
- Define concrete suppression rules + throttle limits + monitoring so we can iterate quickly during Week 1–2 without generating support/compliance incidents.

Scope
- Applies to lifecycle emails sent to self-serve signups and early users during the lifecycle growth experiments sprint.
- Does NOT apply to Sales outreach (Avery/CS sequences), support notifications, or system transactional emails (password reset, billing receipts).

Owners / escalation
- Primary: Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops)
- Copy/targeting: Ben Carter (Growth)
- Compliance + user complaints coordination: Dev Patel (Support guardrails)
- SLO / platform monitoring tie-ins for console links + error spike correlation: Sean Gallagher
- Exec visibility: Camila Reyes

Definitions
- ESP: email service provider (sending infrastructure).
- Lifecycle platform: tool triggering emails (events, schedules, segments).
- Suppression: prevent a send to a recipient for policy reasons (unsubscribed, bounced, complaint, etc.).
- Throttle: rate limiting outbound email volume to manage reputation and avoid spam flags.

1) Sending domain alignment (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)
Status (as of 2025-01-23)
- From domain: updates.redwoodinference.com (subdomain) — preferred for lifecycle; separates reputation from core corporate mail.
- Envelope domain / return-path: aligned with updates.redwoodinference.com.
- SPF: configured to include ESP sending IPs/domains.
- DKIM: 2048-bit keys, aligned with updates.redwoodinference.com.
- DMARC: p=quarantine (monitoring) during warm-up; move to p=reject after stable complaint/bounce rates (target 2–4 weeks).

Checklist (pre-launch)
- SPF passes for sample sends to Gmail + Outlook + Yahoo.
- DKIM passes and aligns (d=updates.redwoodinference.com).
- DMARC passes with alignment; rua reporting enabled to security@ and marketing-ops@.
- Branding consistency: friendly-from name “Redwood Inference” and reply-to lifecycle-support@redwoodinference.com.
- List-Unsubscribe header enabled:
  - List-Unsubscribe: <mailto:unsubscribe@updates.redwoodinference.com>, <https://console.redwoodinference.com/unsubscribe?...>
  - List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click
- Dedicated sending IP vs shared:
  - Decision: start shared pool for warm-up unless volume justifies dedicated IP. Re-evaluate at sustained >150k sends/week.

Open items
- Confirm ESP final configuration after INT-991 changes (SPF/DKIM alignment + deliverability dashboards access). Owner: Tyler.

2) Suppression rules (global + sprint-specific)
Global suppression (ALWAYS suppress)
1) Unsubscribed recipients
- Any user who opted out of marketing/lifecycle (per preferences center) must be suppressed from ALL lifecycle sequences.
- Opt-out should apply immediately (<5 minutes propagation).
- If multiple user records share an email address, suppression is by email address (not only by user_id).

2) Spam complaints
- Any recipient with a spam complaint is hard-suppressed permanently (by email address).

3) Hard bounces
- Hard bounce => permanent suppression by email.
- Soft bounces => suppress after 3 consecutive soft bounces in 72 hours (or per ESP best practice), then retry only if user re-verifies email.

4) Known invalid / risky addresses
- Role-based addresses (admin@, info@, support@, sales@, postmaster@) suppressed for PLG onboarding unless explicitly whitelisted (rare).
- Disposable email domains: suppress (use existing internal list; update weekly).

Sprint-specific suppression
A) Activated users
- Once a user has a “first_success” event (see activation definition in PM-412 / event taxonomy), suppress remaining “pre-activation” emails.
- They can still receive post-activation education emails (streaming, cost dashboard) if they haven’t completed those milestones.

B) High-touch / sales-assist accounts
- If a user is associated with a sales-assist motion (e.g., Salesforce/HubSpot stage >= “Discovery Scheduled” or internal flag “sales_assist=true”), suppress generic PLG onboarding and route to Sales/CS sequence.
- Avoid double-touching prospects.

C) Recent support issues
- If a user has an open P0/P1 support ticket related to onboarding email issues or unsubscribe concerns, suppress until ticket closed.
- Specific: if ticket type = “email opt-out / compliance”, suppress immediately and notify Marketing Ops.

D) Frequency cap (across all lifecycle)
- Hard cap: max 1 lifecycle email per recipient per 24 hours.
- Weekly cap (sprint): max 4 lifecycle emails per 7-day rolling window.
- Exception: critical compliance confirmation (unsubscribe confirmation) and transactional verification emails.

E) Geo / regulatory
- If consent status unknown for a region where we require explicit opt-in (confirm with Legal/Privacy), suppress marketing/lifecycle until consent is captured.
- Current assumption: lifecycle onboarding is “service communication” for account setup; still must honor unsubscribe. (Verify with security/compliance review doc.)

Suppression QA test cases (must pass before launch)
- Unsubscribe from email footer link => no further lifecycle emails within 15 minutes.
- Unsubscribe via one-click header => same.
- User unsubscribes, then signs in and toggles marketing on again => emails resume only after explicit opt-in action.
- User activates (first_success) between scheduled sends => next send is cancelled.
- User receives email, replies “stop” or “unsubscribe” to reply-to => handled by support alias + manual suppression within 1 business day (SLA during sprint).

Incident reference
- SUP-2849: received emails after opt-out. Root cause must be closed before scaling volume. Add regression test + weekly audit query.

3) Throttle limits + warm-up plan
Goals
- Keep complaint rate <0.08% (target), hard bounce rate <0.5%, spam placement stable.
- Avoid volume spikes that look like spam behavior (especially for new subdomain/IP reputation).

Send schedule (onboarding series)
- Email #1 (Welcome): immediate (within 10 minutes of signup)
- Email #2 (Quickstart): +24h if no api_key_created
- Email #3 (First success / troubleshooting): +48h if no first_request_success
- Email #4 (Streaming + reliability tips): +72h if first_request_success but no first_streaming_success
- Email #5 (Next steps / cost dashboard / team): +5–7 days depending on milestones

Throttle guidance (initial)
- Daily cap (total lifecycle sends):
  - Day 1–2: 5k/day
  - Day 3–5: 10k/day
  - Week 2: 25k/day
  - Week 3+: 50k/day (only if metrics stable)
- Per-hour cap: 800/hour to avoid bursty patterns; use “send windows” rather than immediate blasts when possible.
- Per-recipient: 1/day (reinforced by frequency cap above).

Warm-up strategy
- If using shared pool: still treat first 7 days as warm-up; keep volumes modest; monitor per domain.
- Segment order: send first to most-engaged + recently signed-up users (higher open/click, lower complaint).
- Avoid sending to cold/lapsed lists during first 72 hours of new domain alignment changes.

Operational switch (kill switch)
- Marketing Ops must be able to pause all lifecycle sends within 5 minutes.
- Trigger conditions for auto-pause recommendation:
  - complaint rate >0.15% over 2 hours
  - hard bounce rate >1.0% over 2 hours
  - unsubscribe rate >1.5% for any single message variant in 24 hours (investigate copy/targeting)

4) Unsubscribe handling + preference center
Requirements
- Footer must include:
  - “Unsubscribe” (one click)
  - “Manage preferences” (optional, but preferred)
  - Company address
- One-click unsubscribe must:
  - immediately mark the email address unsubscribed
  - be logged as an event for reporting (unsubscribe_clicked) with campaign + message_id
  - not require login

Preference categories (proposed for sprint)
- Product updates (general)
- Onboarding tips (lifecycle)
- Benchmarks + technical content

During sprint, default behavior
- If user clicks “Unsubscribe”: opt out of all onboarding tips (lifecycle) immediately.
- If user clicks “Manage preferences”: allow them to opt out of onboarding tips only (keep transactional).

Support workflow
- Replies to lifecycle emails go to lifecycle-support@redwoodinference.com.
- Dev Patel’s team triages daily during Week 1 launch. If message indicates opt-out request, they must:
  - apply manual suppression (if automation failed)
  - tag “deliverability-sprint”
  - notify Tyler + Ben in #marketing-ops within 2 business hours

5) Monitoring + dashboards
Daily deliverability dashboard (Marketing Ops)
Metrics
- Sent, delivered, opens, clicks
- Bounce rate (hard/soft)
- Spam complaint rate
- Unsubscribe rate
- Inbox placement proxy (where available)
- Top mailbox provider breakdown (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo)
- Deliverability by message variant (subject line A/B)

Product correlation checks (Growth + Data)
- Correlate “email clicked” to product events (api_key_created, first_request_success, first_streaming_success) using UTM conventions.
- Watch for link errors / 404s causing frustration (see SUP-2841 class of issue).

Guardrail alerts (Slack / Pager)
- Slack channel: #growth-sprint-guardrails (or #marketing-ops)
- Alert thresholds:
  - complaints >0.15% (2h)
  - hard bounces >1% (2h)
  - unsubscribe spike >2x baseline for a given email template (24h)
  - support ticket volume tagged “onboarding email” > +10/day above baseline

Weekly audits (must-do)
- Random sample 100 unsubscribed addresses => confirm no sends occurred in last 7 days.
- Duplicate-record check: verify suppression by email prevents sends across multiple user_ids.
- Link validation: top 10 clicked links from each email => 200 OK + correct console path + correct UTM parameters.

6) Operational checklist (launch readiness)
Pre-launch (Week 0)
- [ ] Domain alignment confirmed (SPF/DKIM/DMARC passing)
- [ ] List-Unsubscribe headers enabled and tested
- [ ] Suppression rules implemented in lifecycle platform
- [ ] Frequency caps configured and verified
- [ ] Seed list tests: Gmail + Outlook + Yahoo accounts; check Promotions vs Primary placement
- [ ] Test unsubscribe end-to-end (footer + header)
- [ ] Verify that “activated” suppression works using staging events
- [ ] Confirm send windows + throttles
- [ ] Create rollback plan + single switch to pause all campaigns

Launch day (Week 1)
- [ ] Send to 10% ramp cohort first
- [ ] Review complaint/bounce after first 500 sends
- [ ] Confirm click tracking + UTM params present and correct
- [ ] Confirm suppression counts match expectations

Post-launch (Week 1–3)
- [ ] Daily 10-min deliverability review (Tyler)
- [ ] Twice-weekly guardrail review with Ben + Dev
- [ ] Subject line iteration only if complaint + unsubscribe rates healthy

7) Notes / open questions
- Activation suppression definition: is “first_request_success” the cutoff or “first_streaming_success”? Product is leaning first 2xx completion for activation; need final alignment for suppression logic so we don’t prematurely stop education emails.
- Lapsed user retargeting / reactivation emails: do NOT include in Week 1 warm-up on new alignment changes.
- Confirm whether we have any regional consent edge cases per marketing-tracking-data-review.

Appendix: quick references
- INT-991 (email domain/auth) — must be closed before full ramp.
- SUP-2849 (suppression bug) — verify fix; add automated regression.
- UTM rules — see Drive attribution-and-utm-conventions.
